title: Howard Stern — David Choe appearance (third-party capture)
summary: A third-party capture preserves a long Howard Stern interview with David Choe and a post-interview green-room painting sequence, but begins and ends mid-sentence and is not an official complete broadcast master. Choe disputes simplified press accounts of his Facebook compensation, describes Japanese custody and suicidality, recounts gambling, art, travel and television opportunities, and repeatedly mixes candid self-report with exaggeration, jokes, stereotypes and unverified claims. The record keeps every idea while separating direct correction from host framing, testimony from fact, and risky or private material from neutral discovery. It does not turn the masturbation technique, gambling system, self-harm or escape plan into guidance; does not treat photographs or sexual boasts as proof; does not calculate present wealth; and does not infer permission for either the Chinatown mural or the Sirius green-room painting. The appearance has zero publisher speaker prefixes, so no line-level speaker names are published.

source_notes.claim: This upload is a complete Howard Stern broadcast.
source_notes.assessment: It begins and ends mid-sentence and is a third-party capture. It may preserve the guest appearance plus a green-room sequence, but is not an official intact aircheck.

source_notes.claim: Visible participants make every line safely nameable.
source_notes.assessment: They do not. All 2,826 caption segments contain zero publisher speaker prefixes; quotation, overlap and post-interview production speech remain unresolved.

source_notes.claim: Choe was offered only $1,000 cash or Facebook stock.
source_notes.assessment: Within this source Choe directly corrects the cash alternative to $60,000; contract records would still control.

source_notes.claim: Host estimates establish Choe's net worth.
source_notes.assessment: They do not. The estimates are speculative and Choe later refuses exact holdings disclosure.

source_notes.claim: The host's framed label erases admitted conduct.
source_notes.assessment: Choe also recounts bike theft, tagging and an assault; preserve the contradiction instead of choosing a cleaner story.

source_notes.claim: A large bankroll guarantees gambling profit.
source_notes.assessment: It does not. The described progression retains negative expected value, table-limit constraints and catastrophic tail risk.
The program says company approval must be checked; the capture does not prove approval arrived before painting began.

source_notes.assessment: Treat this as an on-air claim until an authoritative collection/object record identifies the work and custody.
